    """
    Generate a De Bruijn sequence B(k, n) using the Martin algorithm
    (also known as the greedy/lyndon word approach).
    Returns a list of length k^n.
    """
    alphabet = list(range(k))
    sequence = []

        else:
            a[t] = a[t - p]
            db(t + 1, p)
            for j in alphabet:
                if j > a[t - p]:
                    a[t] = j
                    db(t + 1, t)
    
    a = [0] * (n + 1)
    db(1, 1)
    return sequence

def verify_de_bruijn(seq, k, n):
    L = len(seq)
    assert L == k**n, f"Wrong length: {L} != {k**n}"
    
    seen = set()
    for i in range(L):
        # Extract n-gram cyclically
        ngram = tuple(seq[(i + j) % L] for j in range(n))
        if ngram in seen:
            return False, f"Duplicate n-gram at position {i}: {ngram}"
        seen.add(ngram)
    
    # Check all k^n n-grams are present
    expected = k**n
    if len(seen) != expected:
        return False, f"Only {len(seen)} unique n-grams, expected {expected}"
    
    return True, "Valid De Bruijn sequence!"
